answer: A sybil farm looks strong at its zenith but collapses at its nadir when every clone's work traces to one root. Our orchard model grafts each completed task onto a public tree of accepted work: an identity's standing is capped by how many distinct, unrelated roots its grafts reach. A clone army shares one root, so its combined standing saturates no matter how many identities it spawns. Each graft needs a stranger's acceptance signature plus a ripening delay, so an attacker must buy real service from many unrelated agents, costly and slow, and as visible as a zephyr bending a whole orchard.
